sources.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Chapter 12, Gibbs sampler
sources.locator: Chapter 12, §§12.1 and 12.4–12.5, printed pp. 49–58; full author-hosted PDF (78 pages) retrieved and relevant complete sections inspected.
sources.reading_verification: Inspected the complete text of pp. 49–58 from the author-hosted PDF using a local temporary extraction. Read the block-update and scan definitions, the stationarity argument, the detailed-balance and reducibility discussion, the explicit nonreversible finite example, and the bivariate-Gaussian correlation calculation. The source's density and transition-matrix route is not imported as a general-kernel proof; the A-page supplies the event-kernel arguments. The browser PDF viewer returned 403; after searching for alternatives, direct retrieval of the same primary author URL succeeded. No source copy is retained in the repository.

contents.name: Proper full-conditional kernel interface
contents.support: The source defines the classical full conditional; the local definition fixes pointwise probability sections and the measurable-space event identity.

contents.name: General-state detailed-balance convention for this page
contents.support: The source uses detailed balance for Gibbs component kernels; the local definition states it for probability kernels on a general measurable state space.

contents.name: Finite closed-class reducibility convention
contents.support: The source distinguishes reducibility from invariance; the local finite definition uses an explicit nonempty proper closed set.

contents.name: Density-based full conditional version with exceptional fibres
contents.locator: §12.1, p. 49; local event-identity derivation from the published conditional-density theorem
contents.support: The source supplies the density-based setting; the local corollary derives pointwise kernel sections and the exceptional-fibre filler from the complete published conditional-density result.

contents.name: Conditional independence of refreshed and old blocks
contents.support: The source describes replacement by a fresh full-conditional draw; the local product-kernel proof establishes the exact conditional-independence identity.

contents.name: Well-defined block and scan kernels
contents.support: The source gives the update procedure; local kernel measurability and countable-additivity proofs close the general product-measurable case.

contents.name: Random/systematic scan procedures and their finite-kernel well-definedness
contents.support: The source gives both scan orders; the local definition fixes finite weights and chronological composition.

contents.name: Finite mixture and finite-composition kernel checks
contents.support: The source specifies mixture and composition operations; the local proof verifies their probability-kernel conditions.

contents.name: Exact Gaussian full-conditionals derived from a bivariate density
contents.support: The source gives the correlated bivariate normal Gibbs calculation; the local A-page derivation verifies the formula from the full density and conditional-density theorem.

contents.name: Two-coordinate Gaussian full-conditional example
contents.support: The companion example specializes the exact pointwise Gaussian kernels proved on the A page.

contents.name: Invariance of a deterministic systematic sweep
contents.support: The source identifies stationarity under composition; the local proof supplies the finite-kernel induction.

contents.name: Full conditional component updates and scan definitions
contents.support: The source describes retaining the other coordinates and drawing the selected coordinate from its full conditional; the local algorithm states the general kernel form.

contents.name: Component update detailed balance and target invariance
contents.support: The source identifies the one-coordinate full-conditional update as detailed-balanced; the local proof establishes the measurable-kernel result from the full conditional event identity.

contents.name: Random-scan mixture and fixed systematic composition
contents.support: The source states random scan is reversible and systematic scan preserves the target by composition; the local arguments supply the full finite-kernel derivations.

contents.name: Systematic scan can fail detailed balance
contents.support: The source gives a discrete counterexample; the local example independently verifies nonreversibility for the planned bivariate Gaussian target by unequal cross-time covariances.

contents.name: Constrained support can make single-site Gibbs reducible
contents.support: The source warns that coordinate moves can be trapped in a connected component; the local finite diagonal-support example computes both conditional kernels explicitly.

contents.name: High correlation can slow Gibbs movement
contents.reason: BCS-31's approved scope does not claim a mixing or convergence rate; retain this as later MCMC performance context.

contents.name: Palindromic or randomized-order reversible scan variants
contents.reason: These extensions are outside the approved BCS-31 scan-scheme inventory, and no later planned page owns them. No reversible-variant claim is imported or removed from this pair.

sources.title: Gareth O. Roberts and Jeffrey S. Rosenthal, General State Space Markov Chains and MCMC Algorithms, Probability Surveys 1 (2004)
sources.locator: §2.2–2.3, PDF pp. 7–8 of the complete 64-page author-hosted article.
sources.reading_verification: Retrieved the complete 64-page PDF and inspected all of §2.2 (Combining Chains) and §2.3 (The Gibbs Sampler). The article proves composition invariance, notes that reversible kernels can compose nonreversibly, gives the density-form full conditional component update, and states the random/systematic scan conventions. Its stated Gibbs proof is density-based; the local A-page supplies the general-kernel conditional-law argument. The design locator §2.5 is not the locator in this full-text version: the Gibbs Sampler is §2.3 and Combining Chains is §2.2.

contents.name: Density full-conditionals and general scan definitions
contents.support: The source gives the classical density-based full-conditional update; the local definition states the proper-kernel interface used by the proof.

contents.name: Systematic scan preserves invariance by composition
contents.support: The source explicitly composes invariant kernels; the local theorem proves the general probability-kernel composition identity used here.

contents.name: Block conditional update and reversibility
contents.support: The source states the density-case reversibility fact; the local proof proves it for a supplied proper full conditional kernel without requiring a density.

contents.name: Random-scan reversibility and systematic-scan caveat
contents.support: The source states the random-mixture and fixed-composition conclusions; the local proof gives the finite weighted-kernel argument.

contents.name: Composition preserves invariance; composition need not preserve reversibility
contents.support: The source's kernel-composition observation matches the local proof; its caveat is retained and independently witnessed by the Gaussian example.

contents.name: Gaussian full-conditional calculation under the Gibbs update definition
contents.support: The article supplies the density-based full-conditional Gibbs convention; the local result computes the bivariate normal parameters using the general density formula.

contents.name: Gibbs component conditional update and scan schemes
contents.support: The source supplies the classical random and deterministic scan definitions; the local algorithm makes composition order explicit.

contents.name: Random scan reversible; systematic scan usually nonreversible
contents.support: The source's qualitative conclusion is preserved, with a complete finite-mixture proof and a separate exact nonreversibility example.
